samples.summary: Server-side note writers bypass the new authorship bookkeeping and wipe existing per-run attribution
samples.evidence:
`YorkieNoteStore.editText` is now the only writer that attaches `{a,t}` attributes, but two out-of-diff writers reach the same `root.content` Text without them:
- `packages/backend/src/yorkie/note-content.ts:67` — `text.edit(0, text.length, doc.content)` (a full destructive replace) is invoked by the CLI/REST content PUT at `packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:187`. Any `cli push`/PUT therefore erases the attributes of *every* run in an existing note, so the blame gutter goes blank for the whole document for all collaborators.
- `packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:195` — the normal "duplicate document" flow round-trips the note through `readNoteRoot`→`writeNoteRoot`, so a copied note has zero attribution even though its source was fully attributed.
The design doc's "consequences that follow, all of them intended" list (docs/design/notes/notes.md:535-550) covers legacy text, anonymity, deletions and storage, but not these two attribution-destroying paths, so it reads as if attribution only ever accrues. Fix belongs either on the backend writers (preserve/attribute) or on the doc.

samples.summary: Tracker dispatches an extra empty transaction per edit; may disturb IME composition in the notes editor
samples.evidence: `NoteBlameTracker.scheduleRepaint` (packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts:168-181) dispatches a transaction from a microtask after every doc change while the gutter is on. That transaction lands in the middle of CodeMirror's composition handling for CJK/IME input in the same editor that `noteSync` drives (packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:68) — CM6 can abort or re-sync an in-flight composition when a transaction arrives mid-composition, which would surface as dropped/duplicated characters for IME users only when "Show authors" is on. No notes-side IME test exists to catch it (the IME coverage in the repo is docs-only, e.g. packages/docs/test/view/ime-composition-editor.test.ts). To confirm: type with an IME in the notes editor with the gutter enabled, or assert `view.compositionStarted` survives a repaint dispatch.

samples.summary: DOM-free `./node` entry exports the widened `NoteStore` but not `NoteAuthorSpan`
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/node.ts:4-10` re-exports `NoteStore` (which now requires `getAuthorSpans(): NoteAuthorSpan[]`) but not the `NoteAuthorSpan` type, unlike `packages/notes/src/index.ts:1-9` which was updated. A Node-side consumer implementing `NoteStore` through the `./node` condition cannot name the return type. packages/notes/README.md:30 likewise still lists the exported store types without `NoteAuthorSpan`.

samples.summary: Design-sandbox note seed writes content with no attributes, so the sandbox can never demo the gutter
samples.evidence: `packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/canvas/seed-notes.ts:32` seeds the fixture markdown via a raw `content.edit(0, 0, MARKDOWN)`, bypassing `YorkieNoteStore.editText`. The sandbox scene mounts the real `notes-detail.tsx` (packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/canvas/yorkie-offline.tsx:119), so enabling "Show authors" there renders an entirely blank gutter — the design-review surface for this feature shows nothing.

finding.summary: Tracker dispatches an extra empty transaction per edit; may disturb IME composition in the notes editor
finding.evidence: `NoteBlameTracker.scheduleRepaint` (packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts:168-181) dispatches a transaction from a microtask after every doc change while the gutter is on. That transaction lands in the middle of CodeMirror's composition handling for CJK/IME input in the same editor that `noteSync` drives (packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:68) — CM6 can abort or re-sync an in-flight composition when a transaction arrives mid-composition, which would surface as dropped/duplicated characters for IME users only when "Show authors" is on. No notes-side IME test exists to catch it (the IME coverage in the repo is docs-only, e.g. packages/docs/test/view/ime-composition-editor.test.ts). To confirm: type with an IME in the notes editor with the gutter enabled, or assert `view.compositionStarted` survives a repaint dispatch.

verdict.reason: The dispatch exists (blame-gutter.ts:170, annotation-only, no changes/selection), but the finding identifies no broken or bypassing call site, which is what this lens requires. The one site it cites, note-sync.ts:68, is not broken: update() early-returns at note-sync.ts:69 on !update.docChanged, and the repaint transaction changes neither doc nor selection. The invariant the finding assumes ("no extra transaction lands mid-composition") does not exist in this editor: remote-selection.ts:100-102 dispatches an identical empty annotation-only transaction from an async presence subscription at arbitrary times, and that extension is mounted unconditionally at editor.ts:390 regardless of the gutter setting; note-sync.ts:33-50 dispatches doc-changing remote transactions asynchronously as well. No composition guard exists anywhere in the notes editor for any of these to bypass. What remains is a hypothetical interaction between new diff code and @codemirror/view internals (package.json:56) plus a missing-test observation — statable without leaving the diff, and explicitly assigned to the correctness and test-adequacy lenses, not blast radius. Refuting on lens scope, with the always-on sibling dispatch as a concrete counterexample to the claimed invariant; I am not asserting CM6 IME handling is proven benign, only that if it were defective it would apply equally to remote-selection.ts:101 and is not a blast-radius defect.
